entries.title: Adobe Experience Manager
entries.body: Three of Vardhan's five years have been in Adobe Experience Manager. He builds AEM components and client libraries, authors pages with both custom and built-in components, and works with Content Fragments, Experience Fragments, MSM and CA configs to keep content modular. He writes Sling Models and manages dispatcher cache configuration and invalidation. He has led deployments of AEM code across local, dev and QLab environments. He also writes the authoring guides that business users work from, because a content platform that only engineers can operate has failed.

entries.title: Cloud and delivery pipeline
entries.body: Vardhan deploys to AWS using EC2, Lambda and S3, and containerises with Docker. His pipeline work has been mostly GitLab CI/CD, with exposure to Jenkins, GitHub and BitBucket. He integrates secret scanning with GGShield into the pipeline rather than treating security as a later review step. He has used Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring, and maintains a Linux workflow on Ubuntu through WSL.

entries.title: Education and certifications
entries.body: Vardhan holds a Master of Science in Information Technology from the University of Cincinnati, completed December 2023 with a 4.0 GPA. His undergraduate degree is a Bachelor of Technology in Information Technology from Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Hyderabad, completed in 2013. He is a Microsoft Certified Azure Data Engineer Associate (DP-203). He is working towards the AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate but has not yet passed it.

entries.title: Overall shape of the experience
entries.body: Vardhan has five years of professional experience building scalable, responsive web applications, spread across enterprise, fintech, telecom and healthcare. The through-line is full stack work on enterprise content platforms, with Adobe Experience Manager as the deepest single specialism at three years. He has been a dev lead but has not held a formal management or people-leadership title. His stated strengths are rapid prototyping, precise UI implementation, performance tuning, cross-functional collaboration, systems thinking and documentation.

entries.title: What Vardhan has not done
entries.body: Stated plainly so Fit Check has something honest to draw on. Vardhan's source documents show no Kubernetes, no Terraform, no Python, no Go, no Rust, no C#, no native iOS or Android, no React Native, no machine learning model training, and no data science or analytics engineering beyond database work. He has not held a formal engineering management title, and has not worked at consumer-scale startups. His WebGL and retrieval work is independent rather than production experience at an employer. If a role centres on any of these, that is a genuine gap and should be said.

entries.title: Java and Node backend services
entries.body: Vardhan writes backend services in both Java and Node. On the Java side that is Spring Boot and Hibernate; on the Node side, Express and REST APIs. He has built and tested Node REST services and integrated them through a publish-subscribe layer on an enterprise platform. He works with GraphQL as well as REST. Databases he has used in production include PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, SQL Server, Oracle and Snowflake.

entries.title: Location and availability
entries.body: Vardhan is based in Cincinnati, Ohio, in the US Eastern time zone. He is open to full-time roles and to freelance work. Direct contact is by email. Work authorization status is not stated in his source documents, so Fit Check must not assert anything about visa status, sponsorship, or citizenship.

entries.title: ANON Dapp
entries.body: A decentralized application exploring anonymity using zero-knowledge proof frameworks, built with Solidity and React on Ethereum. This is exploratory blockchain work, among Vardhan's older side projects. Source is public at github.com/grammerpro/ANON-Dapp.

entries.title: Aura Landing
entries.body: A landing page for Aura, a concept for AI frameworks and smart eyewear. It is a front-end and visual design exercise in Next.js and Tailwind rather than a full application. Source is public at github.com/grammerpro/aura-landing.

entries.title: Blockchain File Storage
entries.body: Decentralized file storage using Ethereum smart contracts with IPFS as the storage layer, fronted by React. Like ANON Dapp, this is exploratory blockchain work rather than production experience. Source is public at github.com/grammerpro/BlockchainFileStorage.

entries.title: Chroma Loop
entries.body: An interactive WebGL experience built with Three.js and custom shader ribbons. It is a graphics experiment rather than a product. Source is public at github.com/grammerpro/Chroma-Loop.

entries.title: Java Native RAG System
entries.body: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation system written natively in Java, for fast local LLM document intelligence. It runs local models against local documents rather than calling a hosted API, which keeps the documents on the machine. Source is public at github.com/grammerpro/Java-Native-RAG-System.

entries.title: PDF Editor Tool
entries.body: A PDF document editor that runs entirely in the browser, with digital signature support built on WebCrypto. Because the work happens client-side, documents are never uploaded anywhere. Built with React, PDF.js and Tailwind. Source is public at github.com/grammerpro/pdf-editor-tool.

entries.title: React and TypeScript front end
entries.body: React and TypeScript are Vardhan's primary front-end stack across five years. He builds interfaces from Figma files and holds them to the design rather than approximating it. He has integrated TypeScript controllers into an enterprise platform for dynamic UI and backend interaction, and built pages with dynamic data binding, reusable components and shimmer loading states. He writes Jest unit tests and works with QA rather than throwing builds over a wall. He also uses HTML5, CSS3, Bootstrap, Alpine.js and jQuery where a codebase already depends on them.

entries.title: Retrieval and local LLM systems
entries.body: Vardhan built a Retrieval-Augmented Generation system natively in Java rather than assembling one from Python libraries, running local models against local documents for document intelligence. The Fit Check feature on this site is a second, smaller example: a hand-written corpus, embeddings computed once, cosine similarity at query time, and the retrieved evidence shown on screen rather than hidden. This is self-directed work, not something he has shipped for an employer.

entries.title: Software engineer, mortgage finance agency
entries.body: Vardhan worked through 2024 as a software engineer at a mortgage finance agency, a regulated financial environment. This is the fintech domain in his five years of experience across enterprise, fintech, telecom and healthcare. The employer is named in his PDF resume.

entries.title: Software developer, healthcare software
entries.body: Vardhan's first professional role, from September 2019 to February 2021, as a software developer in healthcare software. This is the healthcare domain in his stated experience. The employer is named in his PDF resume.

entries.title: Software engineer, global insurer via consultancy
entries.body: From March 2021 to July 2022 Vardhan was a software engineer working for a global insurer through a large IT consultancy. This is the insurance side of his enterprise experience. Both companies are named in his PDF resume.

entries.title: AEM full stack developer and dev lead, national telecom carrier
entries.body: Vardhan's current role, held since January 2025, at a national telecom carrier. He is an AEM full stack developer and dev lead. He authors AEM pages using client libraries and both custom and built-in components, and integrates TypeScript controllers into the carrier's internal platform for dynamic UI and backend interaction. He built and tested Node REST services integrated through that platform's publish-subscribe layer, designed SEO and analytics, and built a telemetry page. He manages dispatcher cache and leads deployments across environments. The employer is named in his PDF resume.

entries.title: Full stack developer, university
entries.body: From October 2022 to December 2023 Vardhan worked as a full stack developer at a university, overlapping with his master's study there. The employer is named in his PDF resume.

entries.title: SEO, analytics and performance
entries.body: Vardhan has designed SEO and analytics implementations on enterprise sites, improving search visibility and giving the business usable behavioural data. He has built a telemetry page with dynamic binding and reusable components. Performance tuning is one of his stated strengths, and this portfolio is instrumented against explicit Core Web Vitals budgets rather than vibes.

entries.title: WebGL and real-time graphics
entries.body: This is independent work rather than employment. Vardhan builds with Three.js and WebGL, including custom GLSL shaders. Chroma Loop is a shader-driven ribbon experiment, and this portfolio's hero is a generated structure rendered as line geometry with a vertex-shader assembly animation and depth-weighted opacity. He works with GSAP and ScrollTrigger for scroll choreography. He has not shipped WebGL in an enterprise production context.
